title: glycosmis tetracronia
intro: Glycosmis tetracronia, commonly known as the East Indian cherry or Tetracronia, is a species of plant in the family Rutaceae, native to the tropical regions of Asia. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including the treatment of fever, rheumatism, and gastrointestinal issues. The therapeutic actions of Glycosmis tetracronia include anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antifungal properties, which contribute to its healing properties. The bioactive constituents of the plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
